articles.title: Gift Catalog
articles.summary: The full golfballs.com range in one searchable grid — departments, badges, the '/' filter palette, and the product detail panel with live inventory.

beginner.text: Open the Gift Catalog from the Actions Shelf. The layout: a search bar across the top, a BROWSE sidebar on the left, the product grid in the middle, and — once you've added something — the proposal panel on the right.

items: The search box ('Search products, or / to filter…') is focused on open — just type.
Type / inside it for the filter palette: pick categories, brands, or special filters like 'On sale / promo' and 'Commissionable only' with arrows + Enter.
Sort dropdown: Most reviewed (default), Price: low → high, Price: high → low, Name A–Z.
An X appears next to the search when any filter is active — one click clears everything.
Departments — Golf Balls, Apparel, Drinkware, Gift Sets and the rest, each with a live count. Click to scope, click again to clear.
Custom Items — your own service products (see Custom & Service Items).
SAVED — Saved Proposals (your local drafts) and Current Proposals (live from the CRM when an account is linked).
Proposal dock — when your proposal has items, a compact card at the sidebar's bottom shows the line count + running total; click it to pop the proposal panel open.

rows: On sale, or a promotion currently applies
Commissionable — a custom-logo SKU priced on the volume ladder
Custom-logo items show the 1+ tier; volume drops it further
A custom item imported from that supplier
Adds straight to the proposal (tooltip: 'Add to proposal')

intermediate.text: The product detail panel

Click a card and a panel slides in from the right: big photo, brand + category pills, rating and SKU, the per-unit price (with the struck-through 'was' price on sale items), and — for tiered products — the quantity pricing table showing every break with its per-unit price and green savings column. A footer note explains it: 'Per-unit price drops with order volume — quote the tier that matches the gift run.'

items: Promo banner — green pill with the promo's label and code when one applies to this product.
Cost line — 'Cost $X.XX/unit · used for margin' appears once a cost has been synced for the SKU.
Check inventory — a button that pulls the live stock table (Avail / OnHand / Alloc / OnOrdr) on demand, with a refresh icon and a retry on error.
Footer — 'View product' opens the live site page; 'Add to proposal' (changes to 'Add another' once it's in) commits the line.

intermediate.text: The catalog index is cached locally and re-pulls after 24h (Developer Settings → 'Re-index interval'). Seed data paints instantly while the live feed loads, so a brief 'old prices' flash on first open is normal.

articles.title: Customizing an Item
articles.summary: Eight imprint types — logo, text, monogram, photo, alignment art, icons, player numbers — each with its exact controls, plus dual-pole decoration.

intermediate.text: On a customizable product, the detail panel grows a customize block: tabs for each imprint type the product actually supports, type-specific controls below, and a live 3D preview that re-renders as you change anything. The preview uses the real production rendering services — what you see is what prints.

rows: Drag-and-drop or click-to-upload (PNG/JPG/GIF, ~5 MB). Art auto-aligns to the print area and projects onto the 3D ball.

Up to 3 text lines (~20 chars each) · font dropdown: Kabel Dm BT (default), Calibri, Lucida Handwriting, Bradley Hand · color picker (6 quick colors, 75+ in the expanded panel) · size: Standard / Large / Max
7 style thumbnails — Circle, Hexagram, Gardenia (3 initials); Vertical, Horizontal, Diagonal (2); Simple Circle (1) · initials input (letters only) · primary + accent color pickers
Upload a photo; auto-crops to a circle (or square where the product calls for it) with a live crop preview
8 line styles (Star, Thin, Medium, Thick, Dot, Skull, Martini, Wine) · optional text line · separate text + line colors, or a 'same color' checkbox
12 line styles (arrows, dots, stars, chevrons, martini/wine glyphs) · 1–3 initials centered on the line · text + line colors
Theme dropdown (Dad/Father's Day, Drinks, USA/Patriotic, Masters, Misc) → grid of 5–9 ready-made graphics

intermediate.text: Dual-pole (the second side)

Where the product supports it, a checkbox — 'Add personalization to the back' — reveals a second, identical set of imprint controls for the opposite pole: logo on one side, text or a monogram on the other. Both render in the 3D preview. The second pole carries an upcharge (per dozen: +$6 for a logo, +$4 for text). Deleting the front imprint promotes the back one to front.
In the proposal panel, each imprint shows as a draggable pill on its line — drag a pill onto another line to copy the same decoration to a second product.

articles.title: Gift Sets
articles.summary: Wrap custom-logo balls into packaged sets — sleeve, black box, or premium wood with divot-tool or poker-chip kits — and watch pricing flip from per-dozen to per-set.

intermediate.text: While customizing a ball, the gift-set selector offers the packaging options: 'No packaging' (default), a 3-Ball Sleeve, 6-Ball Black Box variants with a lever-divot or poker-chip kit, and Premium Wood 6-Ball boxes. Each option lists its size and the upcharge per set.
What changes when you pick one

items: The 3D preview swaps to the assembled open box — balls and the kit seated in their foam slots, imprints visible on every piece.

Pricing flips to per-SET: the ball's custom-logo ladder is scaled to the set's ball count and the kit's own ladder is added, rounded to .95 — the same math the website uses, verified against production carts.
In the proposal, the line shows a gift-set banner (set name + '6 balls · per set') and quantity now means number of sets, not dozens.

articles.title: The Proposal Panel
articles.summary: Where the quote takes shape: line items, split tiers, inline price editing with tier-reset, draggable imprint pills, the promo block, and saving drafts.

intermediate.text: The right-hand panel slides in with your first added item. Its header shows 'PROPOSAL', the count ('3 products · 36 units'), a Clear button, and a collapse arrow. Each line item card carries:

items: Thumbnail, brand, title, and the line total (right-aligned).
A gift-set banner when packaging is applied (set name + per-set size).
Imprint pills — front-pole pills tinted brand, back-pole tinted green, each with the art preview and an X to remove. Drag a pill onto another line to copy the decoration there.
Split rows — quantity stepper × price × subtotal (see below).
A trash icon to remove the line, and 'N units' at the bottom right.

intermediate.text: Splits, prices, and tier snapping

Each line starts with one split: a qty stepper (−/+ or type a number) and a price. The price auto-snaps to the matching volume tier as quantity changes. Click the dashed-underline price to type your own — that locks it, and a small ↺ link appears showing the auto tier price; click it to snap back. '+ Split tier' adds another qty/price row on the same line, so one quote can show 'option A: 12 @ $6.50, option B: 50 @ $5.95' side by side.
The footer

items: Promo block — type a code or open the chevron to browse known codes (only ones applicable to this cart are offered, each showing its real value). Applied promos render as a pill with the discount in green plus any free-quantity line; the total shows old-price strikethrough + new total.
Estimated total — units + the big number.
Buttons — Save draft (expands a name field, e.g. 'Q3 Client Gift Run'), Load (pull a saved draft back in), Generate email, Clear.

advanced.text: Sidebar → Saved Proposals is the gallery of your local drafts: each card shows thumbnails, name, date, unit count, total, and a Load button (loading is additive — it merges into the working proposal). Hover a card's 'Draft' tag and it morphs into a red Delete. Current Proposals pulls the linked account's real proposals live from the CRM — open any of them into the Breakdown view, load them into the builder, or re-email them.

articles.title: Breakdown & Margin View
articles.summary: The profitability X-ray of any proposal: revenue/cost/profit/margin tiles, per-line margin color coding, cost basis, and price overrides.

intermediate.text: Click a saved-proposal card (or the current proposal) to open its breakdown. Across the top, four stat tiles: Revenue, Est. Cost, Gross Profit, and Blended Margin. Below, the LINE ITEMS & MARGIN table — Product, Qty, Revenue, Cost, Margin % — where each margin badge is color-coded: green at 45%+ margin, yellow from 32%, red below 32%. Click a row to expand its splits and imprints. Free promo lines carry a 'Free' badge and are excluded from margin math.
Where costs come from

rows: Every line uses a real synced cost (from inventory or a custom item's entered cost)
Some lines synced, the rest estimated — estimated lines are marked with an asterisk *
No costs on file; margins assume a default percentage of sell price

intermediate.text: Missing costs auto-load when the breakdown opens; a sync progress indicator shows while the cost map fills in. The footer note tells you which basis you're looking at and reminds you prices are clickable — any price can be overridden right here.

items: CUSTOMIZATION — every decorated item with its imprint chips (art square, type + pole, content, color swatches) and gift-set pill.
PROMOTION — the applied code with its value, or the same type/browse/Apply promo block as the proposal panel.
Margin summary box — Revenue, − Cost (with basis), − Promotion, Gross profit, Blended margin badge.
Action buttons — saved drafts get Copy command / Save to account / Load / Generate email; the current proposal gets Open proposal / Generate email.

articles.title: Custom & Service Items
articles.summary: Build your own products — the full add-item form, cost ladders for margin, style options, and the repo tags that track where items came from.

intermediate.text: Sidebar → Custom Items opens your library as a masonry gallery (filtered to the linked account where one is set). The '+ Add' button opens the item form:

rows: Materials, decorating options — shows on the detail panel
Supplier URL; the detail panel gets View product + copy-link buttons
Drag/drop or pick a file — automatically re-hosted on the company image server so it renders in proposal emails
Comma-separated (Color, Size…); each becomes a picker on the detail panel
Supplier cost, optionally as a quantity/cost ladder — this is what powers real margins in the breakdown

intermediate.text: Items show a source pill — HPG or SNUGZ for imports, nothing for hand-made ones — and behave exactly like catalog products in the proposal: quantities, splits, even style variants. Bulk delete handles cleanup after a big import.

articles.title: Supplier Import (HPG / SnugZ)
articles.summary: One-click bulk import from HPG Brands or SnugZ USA: catalog paging, per-item cost ladders, automatic markup, and a review sheet before anything saves.

advanced.text: In the Custom Items gallery, the '+ HPG Brands' and '+ SnugZ USA' buttons start an import. The flow runs in two visible phases — 'Fetching product catalog…' (paging the supplier's search, page counter shown) then 'Fetching product details…' (per-item progress) — and lands on a review sheet: every found item with its thumbnail, name, SKU, cost ladder, and style options, plus an include/exclude checkbox. 'Save X items' commits your selection to the library, deduped by SKU.
Sell prices are computed from supplier cost with the standard model — (cost + setup + shipping) ÷ (1 − target margin) — so imported items arrive quote-ready with honest margins.
SnugZ needs you signed in to snugzusa.com in another tab first; HPG is public. Big imports fetch many pages — let the progress finish before navigating away.

articles.title: Promo Codes
articles.summary: Apply real promotions to a proposal — the picker only offers codes that actually fit the cart, and free-quantity promos add genuine free-item lines.

intermediate.text: The promo block lives in the proposal panel footer and in the breakdown: type a code, or open the chevron to browse known codes — each candidate is pre-checked against your current cart and only applicable ones appear, with their real value shown (dollar discount or free quantity). Apply recomputes the proposal: a green discount line, free-item lines where the promo grants them, and a struck-through old total.
Free promo lines show 'FREE' in the proposal email and are excluded from margin math, so the breakdown still reads true. A warning appears if the cart stops meeting the promo's requirements.

articles.title: Emailing a Proposal
articles.summary: Generate the customer-facing email: four layout templates, content toggles (costs, images, 3D previews, CTA), and the tracked server-side send.

intermediate.text: 'Generate email' (from the proposal panel or a breakdown) opens the composer in place. At the top, a template selector with four layouts: Corporate (squared, ruled letterhead), Classic (the golfballs.com cart-style schedule), Quote (a total panel over a lined table), and Separated (detached option cards priced individually). Then the message fields: recipient (pre-filled from the page's contact when available), subject (pre-filled 'Corporate Gift Proposal — …'), and an editable intro body.
Classic — matches the website's own proposal email

Classic reproduces the email golfballs.com generates itself: a rounded bordered box with an item / qty / cost / total schedule, orange line totals, then Subtotal → Promotion → Promotion code → Estimated total, the expiry line, the tax disclaimer, and the green 'View This Option' button. With 'Imprint previews' on, the rendered preview photo drops into each line in place of the imprint's logo name (turn it off to show the logo name as text). Free promo dozens appear as their own $0 lines, exactly as the site lays them out.
Content toggles

rows: Includes real 3D render snapshots of each decoration (and, on Classic, swaps the preview photo in for the logo name)
Off hides per-unit prices — for teaser sends
Adds 'This proposal expires on <date>' with a date picker
Adds the footnote about shipping & sales tax being calculated in the cart
Adds the 'View this option' button linking to the live cart (only when the proposal saved)
Adds your typed intro paragraph above the schedule

intermediate.text: The rendered email shows each line with brand, title, quantity, unit price and the line total; sale and volume pricing render with the old price struck through; promo discounts appear as a Promotion line with the code, and free items as $0 / FREE lines that still count toward the pre-discount subtotal.

advanced.text: Sending uploads the 3D snapshots, then runs the same server-side bookkeeping as a quote from the website: it creates the proposal email record, registers it for tracking, and updates the opportunity's value on the account. The cart link is only included when the cart saved successfully — if the CTA is missing from a preview, re-save the proposal first. A toast confirms 'Proposal sent to <email>'.

articles.title: Proposal Checkout Preview
articles.summary: A feature-rich checkout UI embedded in the proposal flow, currently provided for preview and validation only—it does not submit a real order.

intermediate.title: Preview only — no real order is placed
intermediate.text: Proposal Checkout currently validates its form and generates a mock GB confirmation number in the browser. Place Order does not POST an order, charge a card, reserve inventory, or write a CRM order.

The preview is useful for reviewing the intended checkout experience: single-address or multi-destination shipping and item allocation, billing, payment fields, promotions/gift certificates, rep-only admin fields, address suggestions, purchase summary, and animated completion states.
Use the existing saved-cart and proposal-email flows for operational customer work. A checkout confirmation shown by this component is not proof of an order.

advanced.text: The source explicitly leaves the order POST as TODO(backend). A production launch requires a defined order endpoint, authenticated payment handling/tokenization, server-side price and inventory validation, idempotency, error recovery, and integration tests before the preview warning can be removed.

articles.title: Gifting Glossary
articles.summary: Every term the gifting suite throws at you, defined in one place.

rows: The custom artwork on a product — logo, text, monogram, photo, icon
The two printable sides of a ball. Dual-pole = both sides decorated (per-dozen upcharge: +$6 logo, +$4 text)
A SKU priced on the volume ladder instead of retail — marked with the $ coin badge
Tiered pricing: 1+ @ $6.00, 12+ @ $5.50, 50+ @ $5.00 — quantity snaps the price to the best tier
Multiple qty × price rows on one line, to quote several volume scenarios at once
One product in the proposal: product + decoration + variant + its splits
A custom-logo ball wrapped into packaged sets (sleeve / box / wood, with a divot or poker-chip kit), priced per set
A product option that changes the price (Tee Count, Color…) — separate from decoration
The working quote. Saved drafts live locally with a name; 'Current' = the unsaved working set
The account's real proposals pulled live from the CRM opportunity
The margin view: revenue, cost, profit, per-line margin color coding
Where costs came from: actual (synced), mixed (some estimated, marked *), or assumed
A product you define yourself (or import from HPG/SnugZ) — setup fees, freight, special orders
The import source tag on a custom item: HPG, SNUGZ, or none for hand-made
A fixed-pose PNG export of the 3D render, used in proposal emails
The CRM record a sent proposal attaches to, and the saved cart's ID — what makes proposals reloadable and trackable
